name: Number
propertyCopy: Size, corner radius, label, placeholder and the stepper are properties of the same component, not separate fields - change them below to check this field's style and states in the Live Preview.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Number is a text field restricted to numeric input, optionally paired with stepper buttons to increment or decrement the value by a fixed amount - used anywhere the value is fundamentally a quantity rather than arbitrary text. When to Use A quantity someone adjusts up or down - cart quantity, guest count. Any purely numeric value - age, price, a rating count. A bounded value with a sensible min/max and step - where steppers make small adjustments faster than typing. When Not to Use A number that's really an identifier, not a quantity - a phone number, a ZIP/postal code, a credit card number - use Input, since these are never incremented/decremented and often contain formatting characters. A value that should be picked from a fixed list - use Select. A range of two numbers - consider Slider for a bounded range with no need for exact keyboard entry. Best Practices Set sensible min/max/step values that match the real-world constraint (e.g. quantity can't go below 1). Keep the stepper buttons a secondary input method - typing a value directly should always work too. Show units alongside the field (e.g. "kg", "$") rather than expecting the number alone to communicate meaning. Do and Don't Do Quantity+-1 to 20 per order. Steppers for a small count the user nudges, with the permitted range stated up front. Don't Salary+- Steppers on a value in the tens of thousands are useless - nobody clicks up from zero. Drop them when the step is not a unit the user thinks in. Accessibility Uses the native numeric input semantics so mobile keyboards default to a numeric layout automatically. Stepper buttons are separately focusable and labeled ("Increase quantity" / "Decrease quantity"), not just plus/minus icons. Min/max boundaries are announced or otherwise communicated, not just silently enforced.
